concepts.label: ip-vpn
concepts.gloss: A provider-managed Layer 3 VPN service that gives a customer private IP routing connectivity and is realized by one or more device-local VRF routing instances.
concepts.example: The ACME IP VPN is instantiated as an ACME VRF on each of R-PE1, R-PE2, and R-PE3.

concepts.label: routing-instance
concepts.gloss: A device-local virtual routing and forwarding instance that maintains the isolated routing context used to realize an IP VPN on a provider-edge router.
concepts.example: vrf ACME@R-PE1 is the ACME routing instance carried on device R-PE1, with its own RD, route targets, interfaces, and routing policy.

concepts.label: attachment-circuit
concepts.gloss: A logical customer-facing interface or sub-interface on a provider-edge device that binds a customer access link into a specific VRF.
concepts.example: Sub-interface ge-0/0/1.101 binds the link toward CE-A into the ACME VRF.

concepts.label: ce-device
concepts.gloss: A customer-edge router that peers with the provider edge across an attachment circuit to exchange customer traffic and, where configured, routes.
concepts.example: CE-A router is reached across attachment circuit ge-0/0/1.101 and exchanges routes with the provider edge using eBGP.

concepts.label: rd
concepts.gloss: A route distinguisher assigned within a VRF to make that VRF's otherwise potentially overlapping IPv4 or IPv6 routes globally unique as VPN routes.
concepts.example: The ACME VRF on R-PE1 uses RD 65000:101, so a customer prefix such as 192.0.2.0/24 can be represented as the distinct VPN route 65000:101:192.0.2.0/24.

concepts.label: route-target
concepts.gloss: A BGP extended-community policy value configured under a VRF to control which VPN routes that VRF exports and imports.
concepts.example: An ACME hub VRF exports routes with target 65000:1, while a spoke VRF uses target 65000:2 according to the service's hub-and-spoke import/export policy.

concepts.label: interface-address
concepts.gloss: An IP prefix assigned to an attachment circuit's provider-edge interface endpoint for forwarding and routing-protocol communication with the customer edge.
concepts.example: Address 10.0.1.1/30 is configured on ge-0/0/1.101 as the provider-edge endpoint of the link toward CE-A.

concepts.label: service-policy
concepts.gloss: A service policy attached to an attachment circuit to classify, police, shape, mark, or queue customer traffic according to the circuit's QoS treatment.
concepts.example: policy-map gold-200M is attached to ge-0/0/1.101 to apply the ACME circuit's gold 200-Mbit/s traffic treatment.

concepts.label: device
concepts.gloss: A provider-edge router that hosts VRFs and their customer attachment circuits and participates in BGP connectivity with other provider devices.
concepts.example: R-PE1 carries vrf ACME@R-PE1 and maintains iBGP neighbor sessions to R-PE2 and R-PE3.

concepts.label: ce-protocol
concepts.gloss: The routing method configured on a customer attachment circuit for exchanging or installing routes between the provider-edge VRF and the customer-edge router.
concepts.example: On the attachment circuit toward CE-B, OSPF exchanges customer routes between CE-B and the ACME VRF; other circuits may instead use eBGP or static routes.

concepts.label: route-map
concepts.gloss: An ordered routing policy applied within a VRF to match routes and permit, reject, or modify them during routing import, export, or neighbor exchange.
concepts.example: route-map ACME-in is applied in the ACME VRF to filter or alter routes learned inbound, while route-map ACME-out controls routes advertised outward.

concepts.label: bgp-neighbor
concepts.gloss: A device-level BGP neighbor session, represented here by internal-BGP adjacencies between provider routers, over which routing information can be exchanged.
concepts.example: R-PE1 has an iBGP neighbor session to R-PE2 for exchanging provider routing information, including VPN routes when the relevant address family is enabled.

concepts.label: vrf-tag-0x7
concepts.gloss: An opaque vendor-specific VRF attribute stored under a routing instance whose semantics are not exposed by the standard VRF/BGP model.
concepts.example: vrf-tag-0x7 is configured on vrf ACME@R-PE1 and must be preserved as proprietary metadata without interpreting it as an RD or route target.
